policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Word order only: 'Jesus spake unto them' renders either the base or the RP transposition; no ASV note is mapped here.
Emphatic vs enclitic pronoun; 'he that followeth me' is the same English for both, and no note bears on it.
ASV renders the second disjunctive as 'or whither I go' (contrasting with the earlier 'and whither I go'), which is the base disjunctive; RP's connective would give 'and'.
Both readings render 'my judgment is true'; the ASV word does not distinguish the two adjectives and no note is mapped here.
Word order of the particle only; 'ye would know my Father also' renders either arrangement.
ASV has the pronoun subject, 'These words spake he in the treasury', with no named subject; the RP addition would require 'spake Jesus'.
ASV reads 'He said therefore again unto them' with a pronoun subject; the RP addition would surface as 'Jesus said'.
Imperfect and aorist of the same verb both render as 'he said' in ASV narrative; nothing in the English or notes distinguishes them.
Word order only: 'of this world' renders either arrangement of the demonstrative.
ASV has no connective before 'Jesus said unto them'; it renders sentence-initial conjunctions elsewhere in the chapter (e.g. 'And he said unto them', v.23), so the RP conjunction is excluded.

ASV renders a relative clause, 'Even that which I have also spoken unto you', which reflects the separated relative; the WH conjunction would yield an interrogative/causal sense, not 'that which'. The mapped note is an alternative rendering and likewise keeps the relative.
The two verbs of speaking are both rendered 'speak' in ASV usage; 'these speak I unto the world' does not distinguish them.
ASV reads 'Jesus therefore said' with no indirect object; the added pronoun would surface as 'said unto them', which ASV supplies wherever it is in the text (vv.21, 42).
ASV reads 'as the Father taught me' without a possessive; the RP addition would give 'my Father'.
ASV reads 'he hath not left me alone' with no named subject; the RP addition would surface as 'the Father hath not left me alone'.
Prepositional phrase and simple dative alike render 'unto him' in 'They answered unto him'.
ASV renders the second clause asyndetically, 'the son abideth for ever', with no adversative; it renders the connective of the first clause ('And the bondservant'), so the absence here is meaningful.
Word order and relative form only; 'I speak the things which I have seen' renders either arrangement.

ASV's text reads 'my Father', but its mapped margin offers 'Or, the Father' for the same clause, showing the possessive is a rendering of the article rather than evidence of the added pronoun; the English therefore does not settle the unit.
ASV reads 'the things which ye heard', a verb of hearing; the RP reading is a verb of seeing ('ye have seen'), which the ASV text and its margin ('which ye heard from the Father') both exclude.

ASV reads 'from your father', a source phrase with the genitive, which excludes the RP dative 'with your father' (r02). Between the remaining two, the mapped margin 'Or, ... from the Father' shows 'your' renders the article, so the added pronoun is not settled.
The mapped ASV note 'Greek are.' on 'If ye were Abraham's children' states the underlying verb is present, which is the base reading; the variant is past.

ASV's text reads 'ye would do the works of Abraham' (contrary-to-fact, past tense verb), and its mapped textual note assigns the present 'ye do the works of Abraham' to other authorities, so the text is the base imperfect.
ASV reads 'They said unto him' with no inferential particle; both variants add 'therefore', which ASV renders wherever present in this chapter (vv.13, 21, 25).
Perfect and aorist passive alike render 'We were not born of fornication'; the English tense does not separate them and no note is mapped.
ASV reads 'Jesus said unto them' with no inferential particle; the RP addition would give 'therefore'.

ASV renders a present, 'and standeth not in the truth', beside the past 'He was a murderer'; that present force belongs to the perfect of the second reading, while the base imperfect would be 'stood not'.
ASV reads 'If I say truth' with no connective; the RP addition would surface as 'But if'.
ASV reads 'The Jews answered and said unto him' with no inferential particle; the RP addition would give 'therefore'.
Word order only: 'If a man keep my word' renders either arrangement of the possessive.
ASV reads 'The Jews said unto him' with no inferential particle; the added 'therefore' is absent from the English.
The RP addition is an emphatic subject pronoun that English must supply in any case: 'whom makest thou thyself?' is the same rendering with or without it.
'If I glorify myself' in a conditional clause renders either the aorist subjunctive or the present; the English gives no tense signal and no note is mapped.
ASV reads 'that he is your God', a second-person possessive, which is the variant; the base is first-person 'our God'.
Dative and genitive of the same pronoun both render 'I shall be like unto you'.
The RP addition is only the article with the name; 'Jesus said unto them' is identical English either way.

ASV's text ends 'and went out of the temple', and its mapped textual note assigns the longer ending, 'and going through the midst of them went his way and so passed by', to many ancient authorities, so the text is the short base reading.
